text: When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people every word of the LORD their God—everything the LORD their God had sent him to tell them, all these words—
Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to settle there.'
It is Baruch son of Neriah who is inciting you against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans, so they may kill us or carry us into exile in Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people refused to obey the voice of the LORD, which told them to stay in the land of Judah.

versions.text: So Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people refused to obey the voice of the LORD by staying in the land of Judah.
versions.explanation: As worded, "refused to obey ... by staying" can be read as though they disobeyed by remaining in Judah, the opposite of the sense. The infinitive לָשֶׁבֶת states the content of the command they refused: to remain in Judah.

text: Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took the whole remnant of Judah—those who had come back from all the nations where they had been scattered, to live in the land of Judah:

the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, and every person whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
"Take some large stones in your hand and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

versions.text: "Take some large stones in your hands and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בְּיָדְךָ is singular, "in your hand"; the singular also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Then say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have buried, and he will spread his royal canopy above them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; those for the sword, to the sword.

I will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods; he will burn them and carry their gods away. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps his cloak around him, and he will depart from there unharmed.

versions.text: He will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods; he will burn them and carry the gods away. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps his cloak around him, and he will depart from there unharmed.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וְהִצַּתִּי is first person singular ("I will set fire"), matching the divine speech of verses 10-11 where the LORD acts through Nebuchadnezzar. The shift to "He" removes the deliberate alternation between God as ultimate agent and the king as instrument that the Hebrew preserves in this verse.

text: He will shatter the sacred pillars of Heliopolis, the city of the sun, in the land of Egypt, and he will burn down the temples of Egypt's gods."

versions.text: He will shatter the sacred pillars of Heliopolis in the land of Egypt, and he will burn down the temples of Egypt's gods."
versions.explanation: "Heliopolis" is an interpretive rendering of Hebrew Beth Shemesh ("house of the sun"). A brief in-text clarification (or a footnote reading "Hebrew Beth Shemesh, 'house of the sun'") helps hearers who would not recognize the Greek name.
